target_customer: Brazilian restaurants, bars and small food retailers (MEI and ME)
problem: Small food businesses lack working capital to pay suppliers and are poorly served by banks.
business_model: Short-term credit with service fee, bank correspondent model

founders.name: Yonathan Faber
previous_startups: Ridesharing app in Brazil (before Uber entered)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page; also named CEO by Finsiders Brasil.

competitors.name: MovilePay (iFood Pago)
competitors.what: Working capital credit to iFood restaurants
competitors.traction_then: Credit lines of R$10k to R$500k

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit underwriting and payment integration for small merchants, standard engineering with regulatory care.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment history gives some data edge but lending is capital driven and copyable by iFood backed players.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: iFood's MovilePay already lent to restaurants in 2021; Alelo launched a R$160M restaurant credit line in June 2022.

market_need_then: Brazilian restaurants needed short-term supplier credit; a 2022 Brazil Journal article reports the company pivoting from group buying to credit and raising angels.

identity.voice_and_tone: Site promises fast, no bureaucracy working capital via phone

rebrands.why: Finsiders Brasil calls it the now renamed Pantore Pay; date unknown

brand_strength.rationale: Site shows supplier logos like Ambev and Coca-Cola as social proof but no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.to: Credit line for restaurants to pay suppliers
pivots.why: Per Finsiders Brasil; date not stated

outcome_analysis: Pantore moved from group buying to short-term credit for restaurants and took a YC check in 2022. YC lists it inactive, but its website carried a 2026 footer and Monitor Mercantil reported over 10 thousand credit operations in September 2025, so the company appears to still operate and the inactive flag may be stale or refer to a different entity. No shutdown cause is public.
notes: Directory status Inactive conflicts with evidence of 2025 operations; exit left unknown. The $125k seed rests on a single database and conflicts with the $500k YC figure. Education of founders not found.
